title: Sphere Packing in Dimension 4
content: We prove that the optimal sphere packing density in $\mathbb{R}^4$ equals $\pi^2/16 \approx 0.6169$, achieved uniquely by the $D_4$ root lattice. The proof is local: we show every Voronoi cell of a unit-ball packing satisfies $\mathrm{vol}(V_c)\geq 8$, with equality if and only if the active neighbours form a copy of the $D_4$ root system scaled to nearest-neighbour distance $2$. The Voronoi domain decomposes into $176$ combinatorial chamber types, grouped into $22$ orbits under the Weyl group $W(D_4)$ of order $192$. For each orbit representative we produce an explicit sum-of-squares certificate establishing positivity of the angular volume surplus $F_\Omega(\theta)$ on $(0,\pi/3]$, verified by exact rational $LDL^\top$ decomposition of a $6\times 6$ Hessian. A uniform Taylor coefficient $c_2=1/3$ handles the neighbourhood of $\theta=0$, and a Lipschitz continuation (constant $L\le 1.847$; grid interpolation error $Lh\approx 3.75\times 10^{-4}$) bridges the certificate to the full angular range. This resolves the four-dimensional sphere packing problem.
